subject: health
title: Good Friends
about: Kind words, taking turns, personal space and asking before a hug, saying no and walking away, everyone is special, and knowing that bullying is never the target's fault. NC 1.ICHR.1 (healthy relationships) plus following directions and cooperating from PE (PE.1.PR.4.1).
tip: Act out one card together, for example asking before a hug or saying no and walking away.

cards.q: What are please and thank you?
cards.note: Kind words help people feel good.

cards.q: Your friend drops all their crayons. What do you do?
Two friends want the same ball. What can they do?
cards.note: Taking turns means you both get to play.

cards.q: What do we call the space around your body?
cards.note: Everyone likes some room around them.

cards.q: Before you hug a friend, what should you do?
cards.note: Ask first. It is okay if a friend says no thanks.

cards.q: A friend says, please stop tickling me. What do you do?
cards.note: When someone says stop, we stop.

cards.q: Someone is mean to you again and again on purpose. What is that called?
cards.note: If this happens, tell a trusted adult. They can help.

cards.q: A kid is being bullied. Is it that kid's fault?
cards.note: Being bullied is never your fault. Tell a trusted adult.

cards.q: Someone asks you to do something unsafe. What do you say?
cards.note: You can say no in a strong, clear voice.

cards.q: After you say no, what can you do next?
cards.note: Say no, walk away, and tell a trusted adult.

cards.q: Sam draws well. Mia runs fast. Who is special?
cards.note: Everyone has something special about them.

cards.q: Your teacher gives directions. What do you do?
cards.note: Listening to directions keeps games fair and safe.

cards.q: What do we call working together and taking turns?
cards.note: Cooperation means we work as a team.

cards.q: A new kid is alone at recess. What can you do?
cards.note: Asking someone to play is a kind thing to do.
